risks.title: Hydrocarbon price dependency and market volatility
risks.summary: Eni's results are highly dependent on crude oil and natural gas prices, which are volatile and outside the company's control. Prolonged price declines compress refining margins, E&P revenues, and the economic viability of exploration projects.
risks.score_rationale: Fundamental risk for E&P (31-52), implicitly mentioned in forward-looking statements and definitions (12-month average prices). Intense language on economic sensitivity. Stable but structural trend. Maximum weight for a major oil company.

risks.title: Geopolitical risks and regulation in producing countries
risks.summary: Eni operates in jurisdictions with high political risk (Libya, Nigeria, Congo, Egypt). Government changes, nationalizations, contract revisions, or PSA renegotiations, and local instability threaten access to reserves and operational continuity.
risks.score_rationale: Item 1A explicitly dedicated to risks. Eni operates in unstable regions (Africa, Middle East implied). Strong language on contractual dependency and concession renewals. Trend up (geopolitical context 2023-2024). Critical weight for diversified E&P portfolio.

risks.title: Energy transition and hydrocarbon asset obsolescence
risks.summary: The shift toward renewable energy and electrification is reducing oil and gas demand. Eni must invest heavily in renewables (Plenitude) and biofuels (Enilive) to remain competitive, risking impairments on legacy E&P assets.
risks.score_rationale: Implied in business structure (Enilive, Plenitude, renewables). Moderate but present language in forward-looking statements on 'industries in which Eni operates'. Trend up (ESG pressures, EU regulation). High weight for long-term strategy.

risks.title: Increased competition in natural gas and LNG
risks.summary: Eni faces growing competition from LNG producers (Qatar, Australia, USA) and alternative suppliers. Long-term contracts are shrinking, pressuring margins. Dependence on key customers (Europe) exposes the company to unfavorable pricing negotiations.
risks.score_rationale: Item 4 'Global Gas & LNG Portfolio' (53-56) highlights competitive position. Moderate language on 'competitive position' based on market share estimates. Trend up (new LNG entrants, LNG spot market). Significant weight for gas segment.

risks.title: Operational and safety risks in deepwater exploration
risks.summary: Deepwater operations (Gulf of Guinea, Mediterranean) expose Eni to accident risks (blowouts, leaks), production shutdowns, and massive environmental remediation costs. Incidents affect license to operate.
risks.score_rationale: Item 4 E&P (31-52) details deep waters (>200m) and FPSO. Technical language on development and drilling. Stable trend but high potential for incidents. Moderate weight but major reputational and financial impact.

risks.title: Regulatory compliance and environmental sanctions
risks.summary: Eni is subject to strict regulation in Italy (ARERA) and the EU (Taxonomy, CSRD, renewable energy directives). Non-compliance leads to fines, license revocation, and mandatory decarbonization spending. Transition costs are poorly quantified.
risks.score_rationale: Item 4 'Regulation of Eni's businesses' (80-90) and 'Environmental matters' (70-79) are explicit. Moderate but detailed language on ARERA, EU Taxonomy. Trend up (tightening EU standards, CSRD). High weight for European operations.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and critical systems disruption
risks.summary: Eni manages critical infrastructure (pipelines, refineries, FPSO) vulnerable to cyberattacks. Disruption of SCADA systems or production data could paralyze operations, cause leaks, and expose sensitive data.
risks.score_rationale: Item 16K 'Cybersecurity' (184) mentioned but content not provided. Minimal language in extract. Trend new/up (growing threats in energy sector). Moderate weight but high potential operational impact.

risks.title: Dependency on partners and joint ventures
risks.summary: Many E&P projects are operated through partnerships (Nigeria, Congo, Egypt). Financial or operational failure of a partner, or strategic disagreements, may block investments, reduce production, or force Eni to absorb additional costs.
risks.score_rationale: Implied in PSA and concession contracts (glossary). Moderate language on 'agreements with partners'. Stable trend. Moderate weight for co-developed E&P portfolio.
